title: Sesh Domain Architecture Foundation
purpose: Establish Sesh as a bounded product and creative-technology domain within the existing River repository.
Define the canonical ownership boundaries between reusable River infrastructure and genuinely music-specific Sesh concepts.
Prevent duplicate implementations of commerce, fulfillment, orchestration, persistence, governance, identity infrastructure, knowledge infrastructure, and deployment infrastructure.
Create the architectural foundation required before implementation of Sesh Studio, Rhythm, Keys, Control, Pulse, Sounds, Launch, education systems, creator marketplace systems, or Sesh hardware.
architecturePrinciples: Sesh is a first-class bounded domain, not an isolated second platform.
Shared infrastructure remains shared; music-specific business meaning belongs to Sesh.
A Sesh concept must not duplicate an existing River primitive merely because Sesh uses it.
A generic primitive should not be polluted with music-specific behavior solely to avoid creating an appropriate Sesh aggregate.
Canonical identifiers must be explicit and domain-owned.

Public presentation, commercial authority, payment authority, fulfillment authority, rights authority, publishing authority, distribution authority, and artist-management authority remain separate capabilities.
Architecture should preserve future web, desktop, mobile, hardware, AI-assisted, marketplace, education, publishing, distribution, and acquisition optionality.
Sesh must be usable as an independent commercial product family while remaining interoperable with River-owned infrastructure.

No architecture decision in this specification authorizes public launch, external communication, payments, legal agreements, rights acquisition, revenue participation, artist representation, publishing, distribution, or deployment.

responsibility: Creator marketplace semantics specific to sounds and music assets.

seshResponsibility: Define Sesh product identities and Sesh-specific commercial metadata.
Map eligible Sesh products into shared commerce through an explicit adapter or registration boundary.

reuse: Existing release-artifact and delivery patterns where applicable.
seshResponsibility: Define the meaning of Sesh entitlements.
Define Sesh-specific fulfillment outputs such as membership access, software access, sound-pack access, creator features, and future device entitlements.
Provide Sesh operation handlers rather than building a second orchestration engine.
Register Sesh workflows through explicit Sesh-to-orchestration integration.

reuse: Existing deterministic identity and retrieval patterns.
persistencePatterns.rule: SESH-001 does not yet select D1, R2, filesystem, Durable Objects, or another storage technology for every Sesh aggregate. Storage follows domain requirements after canonical models exist.

reuse: River OS may become the private operator/control surface for Sesh business operations.
Existing CRM can represent external people and relationships where its model is semantically sufficient.
Existing analytics, workflow, and operator tooling should be extended instead of duplicated when appropriate.
riverOS.rule: Sesh creator-facing product identity is distinct from River OS operator identity.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshCreatorProfile
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Sesh-specific creator profile representing participation in the Sesh ecosystem.
notes: Authentication identity and creator profile must remain separable.
One authenticated account may eventually participate in one or more creator roles.
Public creator identity may differ from legal identity.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshMusicProject
canonicalSeshPrimitives.rule: Do not reuse generic River Development Agent project semantics for a creator music project.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshAudioAsset
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Canonical metadata identity for audio-bearing assets.
canonicalSeshPrimitives.rule: Binary object storage is infrastructure; SeshAudioAsset is domain metadata and identity.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshSession
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: A bounded period or stateful creative session within a music project.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshTrack
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: A logical track in a Sesh music project.
canonicalSeshPrimitives.note: The discovery word-match for track/stem was noisy and does not establish an existing reusable music-track primitive.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshTempoMap
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Canonical representation of tempo and temporal musical structure.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshBeatGrid
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Beat/subdivision structure against which rhythmic events and cues may be synchronized.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshInputEvent
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Normalized creator-input event independent of input device.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshCue
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Time-addressed feedback instruction synchronized with musical state.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshLearningProgress
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Creator progress across Sesh learning experiences.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshCollaboration
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Canonical relationship between creators and a Sesh music project.
canonicalSeshPrimitives.rule: Do not reuse generic website contribution/collaboration wording as a music collaboration model.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshSoundListing
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Creator-marketplace listing for eligible music assets.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshRightsRecord
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Structured representation of declared rights interests associated with eligible Sesh works or assets.
canonicalSeshPrimitives.boundary: A software record does not establish legal ownership by itself.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshEconomicParticipation
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Structured representation of contractual economic participation such as negotiated revenue shares.
canonicalSeshPrimitives.boundary: Must not imply ownership, royalty entitlement, management authority, publishing authority, or legal enforceability absent valid agreements.

canonicalSeshPrimitives.name: SeshLaunchEngagement
canonicalSeshPrimitives.description: Optional artist-development relationship for creators accepted into Sesh Launch.
boundary: Creator use of Sesh does not automatically create a Sesh Launch engagement.
Sesh Launch participation does not automatically create management, label, publishing, distribution, ownership, or revenue-share rights.
Any such authority must arise from explicit separate agreements.

products.name: Sesh Rhythm
products.purpose: Rhythm-centered learning, performance, and body-to-beat interaction.

products.name: Sesh Control
products.purpose: Game-controller, MIDI, and alternate-input musical interaction.

products.name: Sesh Pulse
products.purpose: Synchronized visual, haptic, audio, lighting, and future-device feedback.

products.name: Sesh Sounds
products.purpose: Creator sound library and future marketplace.

products.name: Sesh Launch
products.purpose: Optional creator development, industry support, project support, marketing, publishing/distribution coordination, funding, or negotiated economic participation.
products.governance: Explicit legal and human approval boundaries required before real-world authority or economic participation.

creatorLifecycle: create account through future shared authentication boundary
optionally obtain premium features or products through shared commerce
optionally enter explicitly negotiated industry/economic relationships

audioEngine: Web Audio, AudioWorklet, WASM, native audio, or another engine must be selected through a later capability investigation.
storage: Metadata storage technology not globally selected by SESH-001.
Large binary audio should not be embedded directly in ordinary relational records.
Audio-object storage and metadata persistence must remain separable.
realtime: Realtime collaboration architecture not selected by SESH-001.
Low-latency local musical interaction must not depend on remote orchestration.
ai: AI is an assistive capability, not the canonical Sesh domain itself.
Future AI features may analyze, recommend, generate, transform, teach, classify, mix, arrange, or assist.
Core creator/project/audio/timing state must remain understandable independently of a specific AI provider.

rightsAndIndustryGovernance: Creator-uploaded content must preserve declared provenance and ownership assertions.
Sesh must distinguish technical possession of an asset from copyright ownership.
Sesh must distinguish authorship, master ownership, composition ownership, publishing rights, distribution rights, management authority, licenses, and economic participation.
Marketplace listing must not silently grant Sesh ownership.
Sesh Launch must be opt-in and separately governed.
Negotiated project participation must be explicit and project-specific.
No platform-wide default ownership claim should be inferred from ordinary Sesh use.
Future rights/split functionality requires legal review before production contractual use.
businessOptionality: Future acquisition of some or all Sesh technology or business.

firstImplementationTarget.title: Canonical Sesh Core Domain Model
firstImplementationTarget.reason: The repository currently lacks direct canonical primitives for the core Sesh creator/music domain. Establishing these before UI, persistence, marketplace, rights, AI, or audio-engine work prevents architectural duplication and premature coupling.

prohibitedByThisSpecification: Accepting creator works under legal terms.
acceptanceCriteria: Sesh is explicitly represented as its own bounded domain.
Shared River infrastructure is distinguished from Sesh-owned business concepts.
Core Sesh identifiers and aggregates are named before implementation.
Creator identity does not silently replace authentication identity, CRM identity, or legal identity.
MusicProject is distinguished from development-agent or generic planning project concepts.
Audio metadata is distinguished from binary object storage.
Sesh commerce is designed to reuse shared commerce rather than duplicate Stripe/payment infrastructure.
Sesh fulfillment is designed to reuse shared fulfillment.
Sesh workflows are designed to reuse shared orchestration.
Music rights and economic participation are modeled as future governed domains rather than implicit platform rights.
Sesh Launch is optional and does not arise automatically from ordinary product usage.
Future hardware and AI remain supported without becoming prerequisites for the canonical core.
SESH-002 is identified as the next implementation target.
